# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible, with register-to-register WNS of 1.387 ns, so iteration 3 must improve that objective to replace it. Iteration 2’s narrower multiplication operands were rejected because their 0.148 ns register-to-register WNS was lower; the supplied seed has no independent routed metrics, so its performance is unknown. The seed’s registered accumulation chain and the violated baseline path’s DSP and carry-chain depth suggest exploring carry-save accumulation, while preserving the fixed one-cycle behavior.

## Hypothesis
Carry-save accumulation should reduce carry propagation in the registered partial-sum stages and may improve register-to-register slack, at the cost of additional registers and LUT logic.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the `acc1`–`acc7` binary partial-sum chain with a carry-save representation: at each stage combine the corresponding signed product with the prior partial sum and shifted carry using bitwise sum/carry logic, keeping arithmetic modulo 32 bits. Resolve the final two-vector sum into the existing registered `y_out`; preserve coefficient parameter behavior, the synchronous reset values, and the exact cycle alignment. Keep the `// @latency 1` annotation; do not repeat iteration 2’s narrow-operand multiplication change as the proposed optimization.
